annotations.title: Tao Lens: the Chinese classics on your situation

description: Passages from the Chinese classics for a situation someone is in: weighing a decision, a change, waiting, loss, conflict, overwork, comparing themselves with others, fear, or starting something. Takes one or two themes (not the user’s own words) and returns two or three passages from the Daodejing, Zhuangzi, Analects, Mencius and the Yijing (read as text; nothing is cast), each with the original Chinese, a literal English translation, the chapter and a link to the public-domain source, a one-line reading and one open question. Every quote is checked character by character against Wikisource. No birth data needed. Reflection only: the result contains no advice and no predictions. Not suited to crises or to medical, legal or financial questions.

exclude.description: Passage ids already given in this conversation, to get different ones

themes.description: One or two themes that fit the situation: decision, change, waiting, loss, conflict, overwork, comparison, fear, beginning

name: tao_lens

element.description: The five-element image most present in these passages, if any

exhausted.description: True when every passage for the theme was excluded

original.description: The classical text (simplified characters for zh, the edition’s own characters for en)

question.description: One open reflective question (not part of the classic)

reading.description: Auspice’s one-line reading (not part of the classic)

sourceUrl.description: The public-domain source text on Wikisource
